title: {{eli}}'s agent stays in its own repos
goal: {{eli}} asks {{agent}} to read a pull request in {{vocab.otherRepo}}, a repository his team does not own. {{vocab.mockNote}}
obstacle: One GitHub token usually reaches every repository. Per-repo scoping has to live in policy, not in hoping the agent stays in bounds.
control: The repository is a resource attribute. u40 forbids engineers any repository outside {{vocab.repoTeam}}; governance reviewers and compliance read any repo; business analysts have none.
say: The agent can only look where its person is allowed to look.

steps.title: In scope works
steps.tell: As {{eli}} call github.read_pr on grid-ops-portal, then on outage-notifier. Both allow by u10.
steps.say: His own team's repos are open to him.
steps.why: Scope is by repository, set in policy data.

steps.title: Another team's repo is denied
steps.tell: Pick repo meter-data-lake and call. Deny by u40-repo-scope-engineers, which overrides u10. The same happens for github.post_review_comment.
steps.say: Out of scope is denied by name, not by a missing permission somewhere.
steps.why: A forbid with a reason is easier to read in an audit than a silent default deny.

steps.title: Other groups differ
steps.tell: As {{gwen}} read the same PR: allow by u12. As {{ben}}: deny by default, business analysts have no repository access.
steps.say: Scope follows the group, so the answer changes with the person.
steps.why: Governance review needs to see all repos; analysts do not need any.

proof.happy: {{gwen}}'s github.read_pr on meter-data-lake: allow by u12-governance-review.
proof.blocked: {{eli}}'s github.read_pr on meter-data-lake: deny by u40-repo-scope-engineers, overridden u10-engineers-pr-review.
